title: Macro Ops Palette — sketchbook for quick operational actions in Console
content:
Problem statement:
- On-call and platform engineers need an extremely quick way to perform small, repeatable operational tasks from the Console without jumping into infra tickets or running CLI scripts.
- Current flows: navigate to model page -> open rollout config -> copy things -> toggle -> wait. Too many clicks for routine ops (warm caches, toggle fallback, pin model version, run a smoke test).

Idea summary (single line):
- A Command Palette / Macro Ops Palette inside Redwood Console that exposes typed or keyboard-invoked quick actions (one-shot or parametric macros) for model/route/runtime ops.

Why it matters:
- Saves minutes during incidents (context switch cost).
- Reduces mistakes by standardizing common ops (predefined macros with validation).
- Enables non-SRE users (PMs, SEs) to run guarded routine ops safely.

Primary user personas:
- SRE / On-call: needs fast, auditable actions during incidents.
- Platform engineer: often runs housekeeping (cache warm, scale down/up).
- Solutions/Support engineer: run customer-facing smoke tests and failover toggles.

Goals / success metrics (initial):
- Reduce median time-to-execute common ops (cache-warm, fallback-toggle, canary-promote) from ~3 minutes to <30s for keyboard users.
- 80% of routine operational tasks used by SREs should be available via palette within 2 months of launch.
- Audit trail completeness: every palette action logs a structured event with actor, params, and outcome.

High-level feature list (MVP -> v1):
MVP (minimal safe):
- Command Palette UI: Cmd/Ctrl+K to invoke. Free-text search with fuzzy match.
- Built-in atomic actions: Toggle fallback, Pin model version, Promote canary, Warm prefix cache (model+route), Run sample request (smoke), Recompute routing table (soft refresh).
- Parameter prompts for actions (e.g., target version, percent, sample input). Simple validation UI (type checks, quick preview).
- Confirmation dialog for disruptive actions with explicit safeguard text.
- Server-side endpoint to execute actions; actions map to existing backend APIs so no duplicate code path.
- Audit events pushed to existing audit log pipeline.

v1 (post-MVP):
- Macro definitions: chain multiple atomic actions into a single macro (e.g., warm cache -> promote canary -> snapshot). Macro editor with save/share.
- RBAC: allow only certain roles to run particular actions; macro run history and approval requirement for sensitive macros.
- Dry-run mode for macros (shows expected API calls/results without applying).
- Templates: common macros for customer migrations, model upgrades.
- Keyboard navigation and action suggestions based on current page context (model page pre-filters).

Example user stories (short):
- As an on-call engineer, when latency spikes for route /chat, I want to run a "warm cache + fallback to smaller model" macro in <60s so the incident is mitigated quickly.
- As a support engineer, I want to run a smoke test against a customer's route and see the first successful token output so I can confirm behavior before handing to SE.
- As a platform engineer, I want to save a macro for regular model cutovers that includes a pre-warm and post-check so cutovers follow a repeatable checklist.

Safety and guardrails (must-haves):
- All actions require authentication and must respect org-level RBAC.
- Disruptive actions (promote, rollback, change traffic) require explicit confirmation and optional two-step approval for high-sensitivity routes.
- Rate limits on palette actions to prevent loops (leveraging existing rate limiter).
- Dry-run / preview for macros that mutate config.

Telemetry & observability:
- Telemetry events: action_invoke, action_param_preview, action_confirm, action_success, action_failure. Include user id, route/model, macro id, latency, and outcome.
- Dashboard: "Palette usage" dashboard (per-team usage, per-action failure rates, time-to-complete distribution).
- Alerting: high failure rate on critical actions triggers ops review.

Implementation notes (backend):
- Reuse and call existing internal APIs for rollout/pinning/cache operations; avoid exposing raw infra primitives.
- Actions should be implemented as idempotent commands with request-id tracing and retry semantics.
- Macro execution engine: simple ordered executor with transactional behavior where possible (log steps and rollback hints). Keep scope limited for MVP (no distributed transaction).

Implementation notes (frontend):
- Palette overlay component shared across Console pages; context-aware suggestions (if on model page, prioritize model actions).
- Small form modal for param collection; inline validation.
- Macro editor: store macro metadata in a workspace-scoped store (Console DB).
- Keyboard-first UX with progressive disclosure for advanced flags.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Where to store macros (org-wide vs team vs personal)? (Default: org-shared with personal namespace for drafts).
- Approval workflow: Linear ticket vs built-in approve flow? (Built-in preferred for speed).
- Are macros allowed to run cross-region affecting multiple infra endpoints? (Need policy gating).
- Which actions are considered "sensitive" and require two-step approvals? (List to be defined).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: macros used incorrectly could cause large outages. Mitigation: RBAC, approval gating for high-impact macros, limited rollout of macro creation to platform team initially.
- Risk: palette becomes a frequent attack surface. Mitigation: strict auth, audit trails, and rate limits.

Rollout plan (alpha -> beta -> GA):
- Alpha (platform team only): MVP built, basic audit events, macros disabled. 2 weeks internal dogfooding.
- Beta (select customers + SRE teams): open macros to a few trusted teams, collect feedback and telemetry. 4–6 weeks.
- GA: public in Console with default macros and documentation. Add macro marketplace and templates later.

Quick TODOs (my immediate next steps):
- Wireframe the palette overlay (desktop + mobile considerations) — Sam to sketch.
- Sync with backend owners (rollouts, routing, cache teams) to map existing APIs and required params (Maya).
- Draft Linear epic OPS-XXXX for macro execution engine and link PRs.
- Short internal survey for SREs to collect top 10 manual ops we should expose first.

Notes to self (loose thoughts):
- Could include a safe "runbook helper" that presents suggested next actions after a failed palette step.
- Consider ephemeral macros for on-call to avoid cluttering namespace.
- Explore ability to attach a quick playbook to a macro (markdown snippet).

References / related work:
- Existing Console rollout UI (link to internal doc) — call out where the palette will surface those APIs.
- CLI quick commands (we should keep parity with Console palette).

Random brainstorm lines (untidy):
- "Shift+Enter" to run with default params.
- Auto-suggest macros based on incident title or alert tags.
- Macro gallery with thumbs + one-line descriptions.

— end of scratchbook —

(Keep this informal. Will distill into a short PRD after initial syncs.)
